title: GPU pod siting & flexible margin scenarios (Q3–Q4 2026)
content:
Purpose:
Call out alternative colocation + on-prem siting scenarios that let us hit Q4 2026 GPU capacity targets while preserving 20–30% operational headroom for power/cooling and a path to burst capacity in EU and APAC regions. Working sheet — contains assumptions, rack-level budget, siting constraints, and action items.

Executive summary:
- Target (hard requirement): supply 1920–2400 accelerators usable for hosted & dedicated inference by end of 2026 Q4 across two colocations (EU/Amsterdam, APAC/Tokyo) and one on-prem pilot site.
- Approach: allocate mix of dense GPU pods in colocations (fastest time-to-serve) + modular on-prem cabinets for sensitive customers. Prioritize racks sized to 18–22 kW steady-state with a 25 kW per-rack breaker ceiling and N+1 PDU redundancy.
- Key risk: some colo sites only guarantee 20 kW per rack on short notice — we need a fallback layout for 16 kW racks.

High-level scenarios (capacity, margin):
- Scenario A (Dense colo): 40 racks @ 18 kW nominal (25 kW breaker), 6 x 8-GPU servers per rack (48 GPUs/rack) => ~1920 GPUs. Operational margin target: 25% headroom (thermal & power).
- Scenario B (Balanced): 30 racks @ 20 kW + 8 on-prem cabinets @ 12–16 kW each (reserve workload for private customers) => total ~1500–1800 GPUs but improved data isolation.
- Scenario C (Conservative/Phase rollout): initial 18 racks high-density + 12 racks lower-density to stay under colo 16 kW limits; phased addition to reach >90% of required capacity by Q4 via two replenishment shipments.

Assumptions (call them out explicitly):
- Average server draw at peak sustained inference: 2.4–2.8 kW for a 4x H100-style node under inference mix (includes host, NVSwitch, aux).
- Ambient PUE target at site: 1.25 (design) with worst-case testing at 1.4 for summer peaks.
- Cooling strategy: cold-aisle containment + variable-speed CRAH units; chiller redundancy N+1 at colo; on-prem pilot uses direct liquid cooling-ready trays where available.
- Power delivery: racks provisioned with dual PDUs, each on separate phases/circuits; breaker spec: 63A/3-phase or 125A depending on site.
- Expected utilization patterns: baseline 55–65% avg GPU utilization across hosted workloads; peak bursts to 85–90% for 1–4 hr windows during high demand (model rollouts).

Rack-level budget (example, narrative-style table):
- Rack spec example (dense):
  - Servers per rack: 6 x 4-GPU nodes (dense SXM or PCIe variant)
  - Peak draw per server: 2.8 kW (max sustained)
  - Rack electrical budget: 6 * 2.8 = 16.8 kW (nominal headroom -> target 18 kW)
  - Breaker reserve: 25 kW ceiling to allow intra-rack maintenance and transient peaks
- Rack spec (conservative):
  - Servers per rack: 8 x 2-GPU nodes
  - Peak draw per server: 1.6 kW
  - Rack electrical budget: 12.8 kW -> typical colo 12–16 kW bucket

Thermal & space considerations:
- Cold-aisle containment recommended for dense racks; measure return-air temperature and delta-T to ensure proper chiller headroom.
- Airflow constraints: avoid back-to-back hot aisles in 1U-dense rows; plan for perforated tile placement and plenum checks at site.
- Lift & install: 400+ lbs cabinets require coordinated rigging for some colos — confirm elevator/cage capacity during site survey.

Siting constraints by priority (short checklist to confirm during site survey):
- Confirm per-rack kW ceiling and throttle policy (immediate deal-breaker if <= 12 kW for dense pods).
- Confirm PDU feed topology and ability to schedule phase swaps for maintenance.
- Verify CRAC/CRAH for containment and chiller plant commissioning windows (summer schedule).
- Verify network fiber diversity options (dual A/B POPs), expected colo cross-connect lead times and costs.
- Confirm staging racks area with 3-phase distribution and charger for installation equipment.

Operational playbook notes (to share with SRE/ops):
- Staggered commissioning: bring racks up 6 at a time, validate auto-balance and KV cache heatmaps per model, watch 72-hour thermal drift.
- Emergency fallback: if a colo short-notice limit reduces available kW by >10% we will shift non-sensitive batch workloads to alternate region / on-prem and throttle hosted inference by 20% on lower-priority models.
- Monitoring must include per-rack power sampled at 1s granularity, inlet/outlet temps, and PDU-level current alarms integrated into PagerDuty thresholds.

Cost/lead-time considerations (notes):
- Late Q3 orders for modular PDUs and in-row power distribution adds 6–8 weeks to lead time.
- Containment curtains and in-rack airflow baffles are a 2-week procurement but need mast installation.
- Freight windows: sea freight to EU cheaper but adds 4–6 weeks; air freight for urgent pilot racks.

Action items (owners & rough ETA):
- Site survey checklist for AMS colo (ask colo ops for per-rack floor plan + electrical single-line) — owner: Aisha Patel — due 2026-03-31.
- Confirm chiller redundancy SLA with colo rep (failure mode analysis) — owner: Lena Thompson — due 2026-04-05.
- Create fallback scheduler policy POC (throttle + model-priority tiers) and test in staging — owner: Dana Chen (eng-serving-runtime) — due 2026-04-12.
- Finalize purchase spec for PDUs and containment material — owner: Marco Ruiz — due 2026-04-08.

Open questions & decisions needed:
- Do we standardize on 18 kW per-rack as the default for all colo orders, or accept mixed buckets and build two packing templates? (Decision by infra PM)
- On-prem pilot: prefer row-level liquid cooling vs in-rack rear-door heat exchangers? Need vendor quotes to compare CAPEX/OPEX (thermal recycling option?).
- Legal: confirm SLAs on emergency maintenance windows for colo sites (can they commit to <4 hour access windows for N+1 failover?).

Notes & references:
- Refer to INFRA-4821 for historical server power tests and the thermal sweep dataset.
- See linked PR for the provisioning playbooks that wire up PDU metrics into observability.

Slack snippets / quick decisions (copied from thread):
- ops-gpu-pods: "If AMS puts us at 16kW we should pre-package a lower-density template — avoids rush re-rack" (Aisha)
- infra-scheduling: "Can we move <10% of hosted tokens to APAC during EU summer peak? need routing rules" (SRE)

Bottom line: proceed with parallel tracks — confirm AMS site constraints this week, order long-lead PDUs and containment for first 18 racks, build the conservative packing template in case we face 16 kW buckets. This keeps us on track to hit minimum capacity targets while preserving operational margin and a clear fallback plan.
